claims.text: Matching the reduction kinetics of Au, Pt, Pd, Ag, and Ir precursors causes the metal species to nucleate simultaneously.
Simultaneous nucleation of the five metal species produces compositionally homogeneous HEA nanoparticles.
Simultaneous nucleation produces a uniform, single-phase HEA structure.
Chelating agents and adjustment of reducing-agent concentration can equalize the effective reduction behavior of all five metal precursors.
Differences in precursor reduction kinetics cause sequential nucleation or deposition.
Sequential nucleation produces compositional gradients in the nanoparticles.
Sequential nucleation can produce multiple phases in the nanoparticles.
Compositional gradients or multiple phases diminish catalytic efficiency.
Compositionally homogeneous HEA nanoparticles have higher catalytic performance than particles formed under mismatched reduction conditions.
The matched-kinetics synthesis will yield a more uniform elemental distribution than the unmodified-precursor baseline.
The matched-kinetics synthesis will exhibit a higher turnover frequency in a model catalytic reaction than the baseline.
The proposed relationship should apply to solution-phase synthesis near 80 degrees Celsius at constant pH and similar solvent conditions when complexation can modulate reduction kinetics.
